clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old female of African descent with HIV infection (CD4 count 390 cells, virally suppressed on tenofovir-lamivudine-dolutegravir) presented with recently diagnosed hypertension and paroxysmal episodes of headaches, palpitations, and sweating, accompanied by sustained elevated blood pressure (160/90 mmHg) and tachycardia (110 bpm). Biochemical investigation revealed markedly elevated 24-hour urine normetanephrine (50,060 nmol/24 h; normal 562–2129 nmol/24 h), consistent with catecholamine excess. Contrast-enhanced CT chest imaging identified a large avidly enhancing left posterior mediastinal T1–T3 paraspinal soft tissue mass with medial extension into the T2 vertebral body and intervertebral neural foramen, resulting in spinal cord abutment. Despite the mass extent, the patient had no focal neurological deficit. After preoperative medical optimization with doxazosin (alpha blocker for 14 days) and atenolol (beta blocker for 72 hours), the patient underwent emergency T2–T4 laminectomy and posterior resection of the lesion. Histopathology demonstrated the characteristic nested (zellballen) growth pattern with capsular invasion and lymphovascular space invasion. Immunohistochemistry was diffusely positive for chromogranin. Histology and immunohistochemistry were consistent with a well-differentiated paraganglioma (GAPP grade 1). The surgery was uncomplicated with preserved postoperative neurology.
